item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 15:00

New York City wants to stop horse carriages in Central Park by 2028. Many people say that working in the city is bad and dangerous for horses.

A bad accident with a horse happens some time ago. A tourist dies. Now, city leaders want to ban the rides. Drivers and workers are sad and angry. They will lose their jobs. They say that carriages are an old tradition. It belongs to New York since the 1800s. City leaders want to help the workers and keep the horses safe.

Many visitors say that it is time to keep the animals safe. There are other ways to see the park than using horses.

Difficult words: horse carriage (a vehicle with wheels which a horse or more horses pull), ban (an official stop), tradition (something what people do for a long time).

item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 15:00

New York City is planning to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park by June 2028. Animal rights groups criticized the carriages for years and said the horses work in unsafe conditions alongside cars.

Support for the ban grew stronger after a tourist died in an accident involving a carriage. While the city mayor supports the new law, drivers and union workers are fighting against it. They say the carriages are a famous tradition from the 1800s and that the ban will destroy many jobs. The city plans to help workers transition and promises that the horses will not be killed.

While some tourists will miss the classic rides, many people believe it is time to stop using horses for entertainment.

Difficult words: union (an official organization of workers formed to protect their rights and interests), transition (the process or period of changing from one state or job to another), entertainment (activities provided for people to enjoy).

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 15:00

New York City lawmakers will vote on a bill to ban Central Park’s historic horse-drawn carriages by June 2028.

Activists have long argued that operating horses on busy city streets is inhumane and unsafe. Support for the ban surged following a fatal accident in which a young tourist died when a horse bolted. City officials, including the mayor, support the phase-out and propose transition plans to compensate owners and protect horses from being slaughtered. However, the proposal faces strong opposition from drivers and the Transport Workers Union, who argue that the tradition has existed since the 1800s and provides a livelihood for hundreds of workers.

While some visitors regret losing an iconic city tradition, others welcome the change and point to modern alternatives that don’t involve animal labor.

Difficult words: inhumane (causing unnecessary suffering to people or animals; without kindness), bolt (to suddenly run away out of control, usually because of fear or shock), phase-out (ending or stopping something gradually over a period of time).

item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 07:00

A new report says that Elon Musk slows down the satellite internet for Ukraine. It is called Starlink. Ukraine uses Starlink to fight against Russia.

This makes it very hard for Ukrainian soldiers to use drones and stop rockets. Ukraine’s president says that the internet is still slow, but leaders are trying to fix it. Some people say that Musk talks to Donald Trump first. Others think that he does it alone.

American politicians are very angry. They want to find out what really happens. They believe that one rich man should not have so much power in a war.

Difficult words: fix (to make something work again), alone (without other people or help), power (when you can control or have an impact on what happens to other people).

item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 07:00

Reports show that Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink’s military internet service, which Ukraine relies on to defend itself from Russian attacks. The restriction made it much harder for Ukrainian forces to use drones and protect cities.

While some leaders think Musk acted completely on his own, others say he spoke with President Trump before making the decision. Ukrainian President Zelensky said that connection speeds are still limited, but officials are working to fix the problem.

The situation made many American politicians angry, and they are now demanding a full investigation. Many people believe that an ordinary person shouldn’t have the power to control military decisions or affect international war strategy.

Difficult words: slowdown (reducing the speed or activity of something), restriction (a rule which controls what can be done), limited (not working fully).

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

item.content:encoded:
27-10-2026 07:00

Recent news reports reveal that Elon Musk personally authorized a slowdown of Starlink, the military-grade satellite network crucial to Ukraine’s defense against Russia.

The restriction severely hampered Ukrainian military operations, affected drone capabilities and missile interceptions. While some US officials suggest Musk acted on his own, other sources indicate he discussed the decision with President Trump and administration members. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Starlink service remains limited, though American officials promised to help resolve the issue.

The incident triggered strong outrage in Washington, and lawmakers call for a full investigation into potential contract violations and illegal interference. Commentators and politicians expressed deep concern over the dangerous concentration of geopolitical power in the hands of a single private citizen during wartime.

Difficult words: hamper (to delay something or prevent it from progressing), interception (stopping or catching something before it reaches its destination), violation (breaking a rule, law, or agreement).

item.content:encoded:
26-10-2026 15:00

Twin sisters Morgan and Lisa move into the same kind of house. Morgan buys her home. Lisa rents hers.

Morgan must pay a lot of money in the beginning. She repairs the house when things break. After 30 years, Morgan pays off her home loan, and her house becomes worth a lot of money. She buys the house for 400,000 dollars. After 30 years, she can sell it for 1.3 million. Lisa pays rent every month. She does not pay for repairs. She saves money. She has a retirement account. After 30 years, she pays 900,000 dollars for rent. But she has 500,000 in her retirement account.

In the end, Morgan makes more money by buying. But Lisa is free to move. She can spend on hobbies, not a house.

Difficult words: twin sister (a girl who is born at the same time to the same mother as another child), rent (the money which you pay when you live in someone’s house or flat), retirement account (an account where you save money for the time after finishing work).

item.content:encoded:
26-10-2026 15:00

To see if buying or renting a home is better, we can follow twin sisters Morgan and Lisa over 30 years.

Morgan bought a house for 400,000 dollars and she used a mortgage loan. She had to pay a large down payment and all repair costs herself. She spent 1.4 million in total, but her house became worth 1.3 million. On the other hand, Lisa rented her house, which means she started with much smaller costs. Her landlord paid for all home repairs, and Lisa invested her saved cash into a retirement account. After 30 years, Lisa spent 900,000 dollars on rent, but her investments grew to 500,000.

While buying gave Morgan a stronger financial outcome in the long run, renting provided Lisa with more freedom, flexibility to move, and lower monthly costs early on.

Difficult words: mortgage loan (a bank loan for buying a house), down payment (the money which you pay at the beginning when you buy a house), landlord (a person or company which owns a house or flat and rents it).

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

item.content:encoded:
26-10-2026 15:00

Using the example of twin sisters Morgan and Lisa living in identical houses, we can explore the financial realities of buying versus renting a home over 30 years.

Morgan bought her home for 400,000 dollars, paid a 50,000 down payment and closing costs, followed by fixed monthly mortgage payments, property taxes, maintenance, and repair expenses. Lisa opted to rent. She started at 1,800 dollars a month with significantly lower initial costs, and invested her unused down payment capital into a diversified retirement fund.

Over three decades, Morgan spent 1.4 million dollars on housing and repairs, but her home grew in value to 1.3 million, which gave her long-term equity and lower future costs once the mortgage was paid off. On the other hand, Lisa spent 900,000 dollars in total rent, but her invested savings grew to 500,000. While Morgan achieved a better overall financial net position, Lisa enjoyed lower short-term expenses, freedom from maintenance responsibilities, and geographic flexibility.

Difficult words: down payment (a cash payment made when buying a house or expensive item, covering a part of the total price), initial (happening at the beginning of a process or event), equity (the financial value of a property minus the remaining mortgage debt owed on it).

item.content:encoded:
26-10-2026 07:00

An Australian politician named Helen Haines is badly hurt. A man in a car attacks her outside her office. She loses a leg in the hospital.

The driver hits her on purpose.  A local barber helps stop the driver. Police catch him. He is 43 years old. Australian leaders are very sad and shocked.

Haines is a kind person who works hard for her area. Australian Prime Minister asks people to stop using bad and angry words in politics. Many people wish Haines to get well soon.

Difficult words: on purpose (when you do something and you plan it before), barber (a person who cuts and styles people’s hair and men’s beards), shocked (very surprised and upset).
